clue.text: I disposed of outstanding firm

indicators.note: read as 'standing out(side)': the word for disposed of stands round the I

parts.note: goods disposed of in a shop have been sold
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having got rid of a company whose payments were overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like 'unpaid' or 'excellent', but split as standing out(side) it puts SOLD around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid and firm are synonyms for something hard, steady and not giving way.

clue.text: Representative bicycle repairer?

definitions.meaning: a person who speaks on behalf of a group
read literally, a man who fixes the spokes of wheels

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical second reading as a man who does spokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spokesman speaks for others; jokingly he is a man who mends wheel spokes.

clue.text: River where elephants never drink?

parts.note: the river of the classical underworld whose waters bring forgetfulness, and elephants are proverbially said never to forget

explanation.surface: A watering hole that big animals avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth drinking from this underworld river erased memory, which elephants famously keep.

clue.text: Removes railings, say, to make barricades

definitions.meaning: takes the fences away, railings being one kind of fence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks railings as just one example of fences.
explanation.definitionFit: Defences are protective barriers; read as de-fences it means strips away fences.

clue.text: Revolutionary 'is outside getting roughed up

indicators.note: something roughed up is knocked about and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the dialect 'is (his) supplies its two letters as printed

explanation.surface: A man's exterior is battered in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of 'IS and OUTSIDE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious speech or action stirs up rebellion against authority, so it is revolutionary.

clue.text: To talk this means business

definitions.meaning: to talk ... is to discuss work matters

explanation.definitionFit: Talking shop means discussing work; a shop is also a retail business.

clue.text: One offered a lift to the course — I wouldn't say if I was expecting anything

definitions.text: One offered a lift to the course
definitions.meaning: a small lift carrying dishes up to the dining room, the course being a course of a meal

definitions.text: I wouldn't say if I was expecting anything
definitions.meaning: a silent attendant who would not speak up even when hoping for a tip

explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests golf or racing, but it is a course of a meal sent up in a service hatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a food lift between floors; read literally it is a silent servant.

clue.text: Tore up letters for actors

indicators.note: the letters of the preceding words are taken and rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone rips up correspondence meant for a cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tore up' and 'letters' paint ripped correspondence; the six letters of TORE UP are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A troupe is a company of touring performers such as actors or dancers.

clue.text: Group of players including scorer with hat trick

indicators.note: a trick here is a twist that disorders the letters before it

explanation.surface: A football team includes a striker who has just scored three goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hat trick' looks like three goals but 'trick' signals rearranging SCORER plus HAT; the players are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing instruments together.

clue.text: Sounds as if a swell is getting worsted

indicators.note: signals a word said aloud matching another spelling

parts.note: a surge is a swell of the sea

explanation.surface: Apparently a dandy is being beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' reads as a smart fellow and 'worsted' as defeated, but they are a wave and a wool cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a hard-wearing twilled fabric, often made of worsted wool.

clue.text: Off school, not doing well

parts.note: off in the sense of away from, out of
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A pupil absent from lessons is struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Off school' as OUT OF FORM, form being a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: A sportsman out of form is playing below his usual standard, performing poorly.

clue.text: Award to wit involved in row

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped up inside the other, so to wit goes into row

parts.note: an oar is what you row with, so row gives OAR
SC, short for Latin scilicet, means 'to wit' or namely

explanation.surface: A prize goes to someone clever who is embroiled in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel but means to row a boat, giving OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oscar is the statuette given at the Academy Awards for film achievement.

clue.text: They are going off dramatically

parts.note: a stage direction in a play script telling several characters to leave the stage together, Latin for 'they go out'

explanation.surface: People make a showy departure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction meaning 'they leave' marks several actors exiting the stage.

clue.text: A couple of matches should be enough for this outfit

definitions.text: A couple of matches should be enough for this outfit

parts.words: A couple of matches should be enough for this outfit
parts.note: matches here are items that go together, and a suit made of two coordinating garments needs just a pair

explanation.surface: Two football fixtures will suffice for this team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' and 'outfit' suggest sport and a team, but the outfit is clothing and the matches are pieces that go together.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece is a suit or swimsuit made of two matching garments.

clue.text: Styptic used in a stable hospital department

parts.note: a string is the stable of racehorses owned by one person
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A blood-stopping agent is applied in a hospital ward that treats horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic stops bleeding by contracting tissue, which is what an astringent does.

clue.text: Primate taking action in evening dress

parts.note: a monkey is one kind of primate
a legal action is a lawsuit, or suit

explanation.surface: An ape in a dinner jacket is acting up.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY SUIT is a slang name for formal evening dress such as a dinner jacket or tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey suit is slang for a dinner suit or other formal men's evening wear.

clue.text: Anaesthetic unit showing the best record

parts.note: an anaesthetic is something that makes you more numb, a number
a unit is one

explanation.surface: A painkiller appears on the top-selling single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anaesthetic' is read as numb-er, a thing that numbs, not the word for a count.
explanation.definitionFit: A number one is a record that has topped the sales chart.

clue.text: Horse slipping its tether causes irritation

indicators.note: a horse slipping its tether gets free of it, so H comes out of the word for tether

parts.note: to hitch a horse is to tether it
horse is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H

explanation.surface: A horse that breaks loose from its rope annoys people.
explanation.walkthrough: The horse here is not an animal but heroin, H in drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a skin irritation that makes one want to scratch.

clue.text: Evening of masquerade creating awe? Hell, no!

indicators.note: the letters are worked up into a new creation, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A night of costumes scares nobody: heck, no!
explanation.walkthrough: AWE HELL NO gives the nine letters rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween, 31 October, is the evening when people go out in costumes and masks.

clue.text: Assembles for prayers

definitions.meaning: short set prayers said in church services

explanation.definitionFit: To collect is to gather; collects are the short prayers of a church service.

clue.text: Not feeling bishop should join union

parts.note: the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers in Britain
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An unfeeling cleric ought to become a union member.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb describes being without sensation, as after cold or an injection.

clue.text: Soldiers in parachute descent causing disorganised brawl

indicators.note: soldiers are placed inside the parachute descent

parts.note: freefall is the part of a parachute jump before the canopy opens
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Troops dropping by parachute cause a chaotic fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is an uncontrolled fight or contest in which anyone may join.

clue.text: Opposed to a division in the chapter

parts.note: a verse is a numbered division of a chapter in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a split in the local branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter' could be a branch of a society, but it is a Bible chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means disliking it or standing against it.

clue.text: Piercing cold on the way out

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
someone on the way out is leaving

explanation.surface: A biting chill as one departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaving means splitting or cutting through, so it can stand for piercing.

clue.text: As winner, fellow secures millions

indicators.note: the fellow holds the other piece safe inside

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Having won, a man locks up a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Champ, short for champion, is the winner of a contest.

clue.text: Start off Burgundy, great amount to get drunk

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a lot is a great amount
taken as written

explanation.surface: Begin with a big quantity of red wine in order to become inebriated.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for extremely drunk.

clue.text: First sign of tiredness isn't an infection

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ain't is colloquial for isn't

explanation.surface: Feeling tired does not mean one has caught something.
explanation.definitionFit: A taint is a trace of contamination or infection.

clue.text: Pull out at a distance from safari

indicators.note: the letters are drawn from inside the following word

explanation.surface: Withdraw far away from an expedition.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means far off, at or from a distance.

clue.text: Run away from tanks to establish liaison

indicators.note: run is taken away from the word for tanks

parts.note: armour is the collective term for tanks and armoured vehicles
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fleeing a tank battle to set up contact with the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liaison' reads as military contact, but here it is a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one, which is one sense of liaison.

clue.text: Impact I have is impressive

parts.note: an impact is an effect
contracted to I've

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their influence is striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something effective produces a strong result, so it is striking or impressive.

clue.text: Compère here encountering hesitation

parts.note: someone here is present
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: The host hesitates on arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the accented letter of 'Compère', which the scan shows in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A compère is the host who introduces acts on a show, a presenter.

clue.text: A fabric demonstrated

definitions.meaning: a smooth glossy cloth woven with a sheen on one side
took part in a sit-in protest, occupying a building

explanation.walkthrough: Split as SAT IN, the second sense is the past of the sit-in protest.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a glossy cloth; sat in means held a sit-in, a form of demonstration.
